transcript.text: Hi, the light in my Neff oven has stopped working (model B1ACE4HN0B). Oven works fine otherwise. Can I change the bulb myself and what bulb do I need?

Yes, in most cases this is a simple DIY job. Here's what you need to know.

## What bulb you need

Neff ovens of this type usually use a 25W, 230V, G9 halogen bulb rated for high temperatures (300°C). The G9 has two looped pins that push straight in rather than screwing in.

However, models vary, so before buying:
• Check your user manual (search "B1ACE4HN0B manual" on the Neff website). It will list the bulb type.
• Or remove the old bulb first and match it. The specs are often printed on the glass or base.
• Buy an oven-rated bulb. A standard G9 from a lighting shop won't withstand the heat. The genuine Neff part is available from the Neff/BSH spare parts website by entering your model number, or you can find compatible oven bulbs cheaply online.

If your oven has LED lighting instead of a halogen bulb behind a removable cover, it's usually not user-replaceable and needs a Neff engineer.

## How to change it

1. Turn off the power at the isolator switch or fuse box, not just the oven controls.
2. Let the oven cool completely.
3. Lay a tea towel on the oven floor to protect the enamel and catch the glass cover if it drops.
4. Locate the lamp cover, usually on a side wall or in the ceiling of the cavity. If it's on the side, you may need to unhook the shelf rails first.
5. Remove the glass cover. Depending on the design, it either twists anticlockwise or unclips. Some need gentle levering at the edge with a flat-bladed tool or spoon handle. Don't force it.
6. Pull the old bulb straight out. Don't twist it.
7. Fit the new bulb without touching the glass with bare fingers. Use a tissue or cloth, since skin oils shorten halogen bulb life.
8. Refit the cover (check any seal is seated properly), replace the shelf rails, and restore the power.

## If it still doesn't work

If a new bulb doesn't fix it, the fault could be the lamp holder, wiring, or a control board issue. That's a job for a qualified engineer or Neff's own service team.

Thanks. I'll isolate it at the cooker switch and let it cool first. I've got the glass cover off (rubber glove for grip) and the old bulb says E14, 25W, 300C, so it doesn't look like a G9. The filament looks broken. Is E14 the right one to get?

Yes, E14, 25W, 300°C is exactly what you need. Your bulb is the one to go by, so ignore my earlier G9 suggestion.

## What to buy
• Cap: E14 (small Edison screw, 14mm)
• Wattage: 25W
• Voltage: 230-240V
• Temperature rating: 300°C (must say "oven" or "appliance" bulb)
• Shape/size: Match the old one. Most are a small "pygmy" or tubular shape. Compare length and diameter so the glass cover fits back on.

These are inexpensive and widely available from DIY shops, supermarkets, and online.

## Fitting tips
• It unscrews, not pulls. Turn the old bulb anticlockwise to remove it and screw the new one in clockwise until snug. Don't overtighten.
• Make sure the power is off at the cooker switch before you touch the bulb or holder.
• If the old bulb is stuck or the glass separates from the metal base, use your rubber glove for grip. If the base is left in the holder, don't dig it out with metal tools unless you're sure the power is off.
• Wipe the glass cover clean before refitting, and check its seal is seated properly.

A broken filament confirms the bulb has simply blown, so a new one should fix it.
